finding.title: Delete or merge user_database_dataclass_core_test.dart — it wholesale duplicates user_database_dataclass_test.dart's 8 DataClass groups
finding.why: user_database_dataclass_core_test.dart's own doc header claims to cover tables 'not yet covered' by user_database_dataclass_test.dart, but both files define groups named Account/LearnerProfile/CurriculumTrack/CurriculumScope/ProfileProgram/DailyPlan/LearningLedgerData/Goal DataClass and both exercise the same toJson/fromJson, copyWith, toCompanion/copyWithCompanion, equality/hashCode/toString, toColumns surface per table with only the seed data changed — the file's stated reason to exist is false, and it is the single biggest file in the batch (1176 lines). Two smaller copy-paste symptoms of the same root cause: user_database_companion_coverage_test.dart defines two different 'CompletionEventsCompanion' groups (346, 389) instead of one, and user_database_dataclass_core_test.dart has a 'Completions insert without profileId throws' test (1130) that is byte-for-byte identical to the 'CompletionEvents' test 9 lines below it (1139) — evidence the second was pasted without renaming the target. Separately, the manager-API tests for outbox, textDownloadStatuses and sacredWindowEntries are each written twice — once in user_database_companion_coverage_test.dart (lines 901-1079) and again in user_database_dataclass_extended_test.dart (lines 1526-1611). Every future schema change to these tables now requires edits in two places to stay in sync, and CI spends time re-running ~1200+ lines of assertions with zero incremental defect-catching power over the surviving file.
finding.recommendation: Diff user_database_dataclass_core_test.dart against user_database_dataclass_test.dart; port any assertion genuinely absent from the latter (if any), then delete user_database_dataclass_core_test.dart. Rename or remove the second 'CompletionEventsCompanion' group in user_database_companion_coverage_test.dart and fix the Completions/CompletionEvents copy-paste. Keep the outbox/textDownloadStatuses/sacredWindowEntries manager tests in exactly one file.
acceptance_criteria: user_database_dataclass_core_test.dart no longer exists (or contains zero groups whose name and table also appear in user_database_dataclass_test.dart).
outbox/textDownloadStatuses/sacredWindowEntries manager tests exist in exactly one of the two files.
`flutter test test/core/database/` passes with the same or greater table coverage after the merge.

finding.title: Add profileId to TrackLearningOrder — the one user_database table with a bare autoincrement PK, and make audit's claimed profileId check doesn't exist

evidence.quote:
final insertable = TrackLearningOrderCompanion.custom(
        trackId: const Variable(1),
**Enforcement:** `make audit` flags any user-DB table without a `profileId` column.

finding.why: Both test files in this batch construct TrackLearningOrderCompanion.insert()/.custom() with only trackId/sefariaRef/sortOrder — never profileId — because lib/core/database/tables/track_learning_order.dart has no profileId column at all (confirmed by direct read: bare autoIncrement `id`, only trackId + sefariaRef + sortOrder, uniqueKeys is {trackId, sefariaRef}). Every sibling user-data table in the batch's test evidence (bookmarks, goals, daily_plans, learning_order, streak_events, completion_events, stage_definitions, ...) carries an explicit profileId. Isolation for this table depends entirely on trackId never being confused across profiles; a caching or profile-switch bug elsewhere that reuses a stale trackId would silently read/write another profile's (e.g. a sibling child's) custom text ordering with no schema-level guard to catch it. This gap is currently invisible: `grep -n profileId learning_tracker/Makefile` returns zero matches, so none of the 22 `make audit` checks actually implements the check the standards doc says exists — the rule is marked [E] (Enforced) but enforces nothing for this table.
finding.recommendation: Add a profileId IntColumn (FK to learner_profiles, cascade delete) to TrackLearningOrder, fold it into the uniqueKeys constraint with trackId/sefariaRef, ship it as a schemaVersion bump per DB-4 discipline (migration step + schema export + migration test), and update the DAO. Separately, write the actual `make audit` grep the doc already claims exists so this class of gap is caught mechanically going forward.
acceptance_criteria: lib/core/database/tables/track_learning_order.dart has a profileId column referencing learner_profiles, with a migration step and committed schema export at the new schemaVersion.

A `make audit` check greps every table in lib/core/database/tables/*.dart used by UserDatabase and fails if profileId is absent (unless the table is on a documented content-table exemption list), closing the doc/reality gap at docs/coding-standards.md:689.

finding.title: Replace throwsA(anything) with a typed matcher in 20 validateIntegrity insert tests
finding.why: throwsA(anything) is satisfied by any thrown object — a NoSuchMethodError from an unrelated null-dereference, a StateError from wrong DB state, or the intended Drift required-field validation all pass identically. These 20 tests (17 in user_database_dataclass_core_test.dart, 3 in user_database_companion_coverage_test.dart) assert only that insert() didn't silently succeed, not that Drift's required-field validation is what actually fired; a regression that made that validation silently no-op while something else in the same call happened to throw would still report green.
finding.recommendation: Replace `throwsA(anything)` with `throwsA(isA<InvalidDataException>())` (or whatever concrete type Drift's generated validateIntegrity throws) at all 20 sites.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -rn 'throwsA(anything)' learning_tracker/test/core/database/` returns zero matches in these two files.
Each replaced matcher is exercised by a corresponding red-first run (assert it still fails if the required-field check is removed from the source table).

finding.title: Replace seed_manager_test.dart's 7 silent early-return guards with an explicit precondition instead of a vacuous pass

evidence.quote:
if (oldVersion <= 0) {
        // Unlikely, but skip gracefully if bundledSeedVersion == 1.

finding.why: bundledSeedVersion is 15 today (lib/core/database/seed_version.dart:13), so `if (oldVersion <= 0) return;` never fires and every guarded test body runs its real assertions — but the guard is copy-pasted 7 times (lines 176, 200, 212, 223, 236, 694, 758) as unconditional insurance against bundledSeedVersion ever dropping to 1. If that ever happens, up to 7 tests covering version-mismatch rollback, replacing-content-db logging, upgrade/extract-failed logging, rolled-back logging, and boundary behavior silently report PASS having executed zero assertions, with no `skip:` marker in test output to reveal it.
finding.recommendation: Replace the 7 repeated guards with a single documented precondition (e.g. a top-of-file `assert(bundledSeedVersion > 1, 'these tests assume bundledSeedVersion > 1')` or restructure the version arithmetic) so a future bundledSeedVersion of 1 fails loudly instead of vacuously passing.
acceptance_criteria: No test in seed_manager_test.dart can complete with zero assertions executed when bundledSeedVersion <= 1; either the file fails fast via assert, or the affected tests use `skip:` with a stated reason so it's visible in test output.

finding.title: Delete or rewrite the 474 row-existence-only Drift Manager-API tests in test/core/database/user_database_managers_*_test.dart — none can detect an ordering or filtering regression
finding.rule: TQ-8 (tautological tests / assertions weaker than what the source can do wrong) + Feathers lens (test has no seam to the behavior it claims to cover)
finding.area: test/core/database (Drift generated Manager API coverage tests)

evidence.quote:
/// OrderBy + filter coverage for all remaining uncovered ColumnOrderings and
/// ColumnFilters getters in user_database.g.dart.
// createdAt defaults to currentDateAndTime; just verify the filter compiles and executes

/// Additional coverage for annotation composer getters that were missed in
/// the first computed fields test — focuses on fields like id, profileId,

/// Coverage for annotation composer ($$XxxAnnotationComposer) getters
/// in user_database.g.dart.

finding.why: Every one of these 474 tests inserts exactly one row in setUp, then calls orderBy/filter/computedField/withFields and asserts only `hasLength(1)`/`isNotEmpty`/`isA<List<...>>`. Confirmed by exhaustive grep: zero occurrences anywhere in the 2435-line orderby file of `hasLength(0)`, `hasLength(2)`, or `equals([...])` — no test ever inserts a second, differently-ordered or non-matching row, so a broken `.asc()`/`.desc()` (or a filter predicate that matches everything, or one that silently no-ops) still returns the single seeded row and the test stays green. Ran both the smallest (crossref_filter_test.dart) and largest (orderby_test.dart) files in this session: 26/26 and 283/283 pass today, so this is 474 currently-green CI checkmarks that give zero regression protection for the very ordering/filtering behavior their names promise. Compounding it: `grep -rl '\.managers\.' lib/` returns 0 files — the Drift-generated Manager API under test (`db.managers.*`) has no caller anywhere in production code; the app queries through hand-written DAOs instead. This is ~5900 lines of test code (this batch alone) written to drive `flutter test --coverage` numbers up against a generated-code surface the app never exercises, at real cost: CI/build time on every run, and reviewer/agent attention budget on every future change to user_database.dart (per AG-3's own rationale about per-file read budgets).
finding.recommendation: Delete this suite — `db.managers.*` has no production caller, so there is no behavior left to protect. If the underlying goal was raising `user_database.g.dart` line-coverage numbers, exclude generated files from the coverage gate instead (e.g. `lcov --remove coverage/lcov.info '*.g.dart' '*.freezed.dart'` in the coverage make target) rather than writing assertion-free tests. If any ordering/filtering behavior here genuinely needs protecting because a DAO wraps it, move that coverage to the DAO's own test file with real assertions: insert ≥2 rows with distinct sort keys and assert exact order via `equals([...])`, and insert ≥1 matching + ≥1 non-matching row per filter test and assert the non-matching row is excluded.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -rn 'db.managers' test/core/database/user_database_managers_*_test.dart` returns nothing (files deleted), OR every remaining orderBy test seeds ≥2 rows with distinct values and asserts exact order, and every remaining filter test seeds ≥1 excluded row and asserts it's excluded.
Coverage tooling (`make test` / CI) excludes `*.g.dart` and `*.freezed.dart` from the coverage report, removing the incentive that produced this suite.
`flutter test --coverage` line count for `test/core/database/` drops by roughly the amount removed, verifiable via `wc -l` before/after in the PR diff.
